key_insight: PAC-ACT adds reinforcement-learning post-training to pretrained Action Chunking Transformers, improving contact-rich robot control without giving up the low-latency, low-memory benefits of ACT policies.
engineering_relevance: This is directly relevant for industrial manipulation systems that need safer force control and better robustness to pose perturbations in real time.
method: Reformulates policy optimization at the action-chunk level for ACT.
Uses an ACT-transferred actor-critic architecture for online fine-tuning.
Adds a hybrid behavior-prior constraint to preserve the pretrained action distribution during RL.
Targets sparse-reward, contact-rich industrial tasks with randomized initial poses.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved task success, contact stability, and force safety on industrial benchmarks, including a 46× reduction in force readings above 60 N on the Contour task.
watch_item: Online reinforcement-learning post-training may require careful tuning of the behavior-prior constraint to avoid destabilizing the pretrained policy or hurting real-world safety.
paper_title: PAC-ACT: Post-training Actor-Critic for Action Chunking Transformers
